#   Tor Exit Node Blocklist
#   
#   This list contains known Tor exit node IP addresses used to route
#   anonymized traffic from the Tor network to the public internet.
#   
#   Tor exit nodes are the final relay point in the Tor network where
#   encrypted traffic is decrypted and forwarded to its destination.
#   As a result, the destination server sees the exit node IP rather
#   than the original client IP.
#   
#   While Tor is a legitimate tool, it is also frequently abused for 
#   malicious activity due to its anonymity.
#   
#   This list is commonly used to restrict or filter traffic from
#   Tor exit nodes for security, abuse prevention, and risk reduction
#   purposes.
#   
#   Typical activities originating from Tor exit nodes may include:
#      - Credential stuffing and brute-force attempts
#      - Web application scanning and exploitation attempts
#      - Spam and automated bot traffic
#      - Fraudulent account creation
#      - Data scraping and reconnaissance
#   
#   Blocking Tor exit nodes will prevent access from the public Tor
#   network but will not affect internal Tor routing or non-exit relays.
#   
#   This list is sourced from publicly available Tor network data and
#   updated regularly as exit nodes change frequently.
